summary.text: 69-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension who presented on May 30, 2022 with worsening bilateral lower limb edema and elevated creatinine, was diagnosed with chronic renal failure and started hemodialysis with LMWH on May 31, 2022.

An AVF was created on June 6, 2022; thrombosis and occlusion of the AVF was recorded on June 10, and the thrombus was surgically removed with a Fogarty catheter and the AVF reconstructed (surgery date not stated). LMWH was increased to 4100 IU on June 13 for circuit clotting, and platelets fell to 42 on June 15 and 50 on June 20.

On June 20, 2022 during hemodialysis she had an acute allergic reaction with sweating, chest tightness, dyspnea, hoarseness and SpO2 86%, treated with intravenous dexamethasone and oxygen; symptoms improved within two minutes.

The 4T score was 8 and the HIT IgG antibody was positive (optical density 1.64), confirming HIT. LMWH was stopped, citrate was used, and argatroban started June 27, 2022; rivaroxaban 15 mg twice daily was added July 22, 2022.

Platelets recovered (180 on June 26, 2022), argatroban was later stopped with hemodialysis proceeding smoothly, access was converted to an autogenous left forearm AVF on January 18, 2023, and no further AVF thrombosis or systemic reaction occurred.
